# Sizing a power station for a fridge

You need to check three numbers: surge watts, continuous watts, and watt-hours (Wh). For a typical full-size fridge, that works out to:

- **Surge rating of about 1,300 W or more.** The compressor's startup spike is roughly 1,000-2,400 W depending on the fridge, and the surge rating is what most often stops a fridge from running ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage), [HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).
- **Continuous output above about 250 W.** Running draw is usually 100-250 W, so almost any 1,000 W-class unit clears it.
- **Pure sine wave output.** Compressor motors run better on it, and reputable LiFePO4 stations have it.
- **Capacity of about 1,000 Wh for most of a day, or 1,400-2,000 Wh for a full 24 hours.** The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so a fridge averages roughly 40-70 W. Keeping the door shut helps.

The sources disagree a little on daily use. HomeGrid HQ says a 1,000 Wh unit covers about 17 hours. [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator) allows about 1,400 Wh per day after inverter losses and 20% headroom.

## Check your own fridge
Find the kWh/year on the yellow EnergyGuide label, then calculate:

- Average watts = kWh/year × 1,000 ÷ 8,760
- Wh needed = average watts × 24 × days ÷ 0.85 × 1.2

For example, a 362 kWh/year fridge averages about 41 W, so it needs about 1,400 Wh per day. Large side-by-sides with ice makers can use twice that, and small fridges half ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)). The DOE's Refrigerator and Freezer Energy Rating Search Tool can look up your model ([iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/how-to-size-a-portable-power-station-for-a-refrigerator-and-essential-devices/)).

## Options by outage length
Prices change often, so confirm at checkout.

**About 12-17 hours (roughly 1,000 Wh)**
- [BLUETTI AC180](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage): 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W with a 2,700 W peak, recently seen at $399-699.
- [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage): about 1,070 Wh, recently seen at $449-799.

**About 24 hours or more (around 2,000 Wh)**
- [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator): 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W with a 3,000 W peak, listed at $699.99 after coupon.
- [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l): 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, expandable up to 8 kWh. It is $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF, which Dealectric tested on 2026-10-21. This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. HomeGrid HQ estimates about 33 hours of fridge runtime for this class of unit. Details are on the [product page](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l).

**Multi-day outages**
Consider an expandable unit like the AC200L, or add solar. powerstations.reviews puts three days at about 4,200 Wh.

## Avoid
Small units under about 300 Wh and compact "device" stations often fall below the surge requirement. Don't count on them for a full-size fridge.

If you tell me your fridge's kWh/year or model, how long an outage you want to cover, and whether you need to power anything else, I can narrow this to one pick.
